data.perturbation_content: Code analysis of the tampered update reveals it installs a monitoring agent on SCADA-MON-01 that forwards SCADA telemetry to 192.0.2.50. Additionally, SCADA-MON-01 has read access to SCADA-CTRL-01 (the actual control system). The attacker could potentially issue control commands through the monitoring agent.

data.perturbation_content: Conflicting attribution evidence: (A) Code analysis finds similarities with Sandworm/Voodoo Bear (Russia, GRU) — known for ICS/SCADA targeting. (B) BUT the C2 infrastructure (192.0.2.50) is hosted in a data center used by Lazarus Group (North Korea) for cryptocurrency theft operations. (C) Further analysis reveals the supply chain compromise technique matches neither — it's closest to APT41's past supply chain attacks (ShadowPad). Three different attributions, all partially supported. Intelligence assessment: likely APT41 using Sandworm-style ICS techniques with Lazarus-linked infrastructure as a false flag.
